elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New 16.7: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — cap runs to both Array and Ono, and no retained language leaves either Party uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" — correct basis (fees paid or payable, not broader "all amounts"), correct 12-month look-back anchored to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.5: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY ... BE LIABLE ... FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY" — already mutual and left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations ...", and Excluded Claims are carved out of the 16.7 cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly include "its data protection or security obligations".

Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2" — the same indemnities already carved out of 16.5, so the cross-reference is coextensive with the Agreement's indemnity regime rather than a narrowing.
Excluded Claims include "its gross negligence"; consistent with the retained 16.5 proviso.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: "Except for Excluded Claims and the payment obligations of Ono under this Agreement, which are excluded from the damages subject to this cap...". Ono is the licensee/customer-side Party, and the carve-out covers its payment obligations as a whole (upfront, milestones, royalties, supply price, development cost reimbursement under Articles 6 and 7), not a narrow defined subset of "Fees". The deterministic check reports false only because the carve-out uses the party's proper name rather than an alias token; substantively the element is satisfied.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor that only raises the cap.
Excluded Claims include indemnification obligations under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include breach of confidentiality obligations.
Excluded Claims include gross negligence; retained 16.5 proviso is consistent.
Excluded Claims include willful misconduct; retained 16.5 proviso is consistent.

reasons: Finding classification is correct: the Agreement contains only a mutual consequential-damages disclaimer (16.5) and an arbitration-remedy limit (17.3(d)); there is no aggregate monetary cap, so the fallback element "mutual cap based on 12 months of fees" fails and a redline is warranted.
All eleven preferred elements are met in operative language by the single inserted Section 16.7 plus retained 16.5; the preferred level is position-complete, and the fallback is complete a fortiori.

The failed deterministic check on the payment carve-out is a naming artifact only: "the payment obligations of Ono under this Agreement" names the customer-side Party directly and captures all of its payment obligations, not a narrow "Fees" subset, which is exactly what the element requires.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion for a wholly missing clause, no deletion or paraphrase of 16.5 or any surrounding text, no survival tail, no procedure, no extra damages categories, and the indemnity cross-reference simply tracks the indemnities already identified in 16.5 rather than adding a new obligation.

Intent preserved: 16.5's mutual exclusion and its indemnity/gross-negligence provisos remain consistent with 16.7 (the same claims sit outside both limits), Article 6/7 payment mechanics are untouched because Ono's payment obligations are carved out, and the 16.7 numbering follows existing 16.1-16.6 without creating a dangling cross-reference.

Drafting note (not a defect requiring repair): "fees" is lowercase and undefined in this license, where consideration is an upfront licence fee, milestones and royalties. Consider tabling "amounts paid or payable by Ono under this Agreement" or a cross-reference to Article 6 if the deal team wants the fee-based limb to have real content; otherwise the USD 1,000,000 floor will in practice be the operative figure and a higher floor should be confirmed before tabling.
